title: Implement shopping list append service
description: Create the orchestration layer for reading a target file, scaling and aggregating a recipe, appending the Meals provenance entry, choosing flat versus aisle-aware append mode, and writing the result back for both existing and newly created lists.
acceptance_criteria: Service logic supports append-to-existing and create-new-list flows using `ShoppingListFiles` helpers.
Append mode detection distinguishes aisle-backed lists from flat lists using checklist-bearing `##` sections.
Existing flat lists stay flat, while new lists use aggregator-produced aisle structure.
The service writes the provenance bullet before appending items and reports the aggregated item count for confirmation UX.

handoff_summary.completed: Created CookbookApp/ShoppingLists/AddToShoppingListService.swift with: (1) `append()` — reads file, scales+aggregates recipe, detects flat vs aisle mode, writes provenance bullet, appends items, writes back, returns item count; (2) `create()` — resolves subfolder URL, guards against existing filename, builds ShoppingList in memory with initial H1, writes provenance bullet, always uses aisle-aware append for new lists, single write; (3) `isAisleBacked()` — checks for `##` sections containing `- [ ]`/`- [x]` lines (excludes `## Meals` and prose sections correctly); (4) `writeItems()` — private helper dispatching to `appendItem(_:toAisle:)` or flat `appendItem(_:)` based on aisleMode flag. Build succeeded.
handoff_summary.remaining: Downstream: UI integration (AddToShoppingListSheet view), RecipeBottomBar parameterisation, confirmation overlay — these are separate beads within the same feature. Tester bead will cover: isAisleBacked detection edge cases (Meals section excluded, flat list, no headings, aisle section with items), create duplicate name guard, item count accuracy, provenance idempotency via appendMealsBullet.
handoff_summary.risks: ShoppingListFiles.writeText brackets security-scoped access on the file URL itself; for brand-new file URLs (not security-scoped bookmarks), startAccessingSecurityScopedResource returns false and write proceeds via inherited folder scope. If the folder scope is not active at the call site, writes to new files will fail with a permission error. Callers must ensure the folder bookmark is active.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester bead should cover AddToShoppingListService: isAisleBacked with flat/aisle/Meals-only/prose inputs; create duplicate name guard; append item count accuracy; provenance bullet idempotency; new-list always-aisle mode.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. AddToShoppingListService.swift is a new file; no existing files were modified. Downstream UI integration beads (AddToShoppingListSheet, RecipeBottomBar) will need to import and call this service but do not touch the same file.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Service is a caseless enum (namespace pattern, consistent with ShoppingListLineFormatter and ShoppingListFiles). `isAisleBacked` is internal rather than private to enable direct unit testing without test helpers. `create()` builds the full ShoppingList in memory before a single write call (more atomic than two writes). Provenance format `"**\(recipeName)**"` (bold markdown) is injected by the service per spec — callers pass the pre-resolved display name.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: isAisleBacked: test flat list (no ## headings), Meals-only (## Meals with bullet, no checklist), aisle-backed (## produce with - [ ] apple), mixed prose+aisle. append: item count return, provenance bullet written before items, flat mode preserves no ## injection. create: listAlreadyExists on duplicate name, aisle structure always applied, initial H1 present in output.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: File-existence check in `create()` uses `ShoppingListFiles.readText` returning nil as a proxy for non-existence. A nil return could also indicate a read permission error on an existing file — in that case `create()` would proceed and overwrite the file. This is an acceptable trade-off given the narrow scenario and consistent with the rest of the codebase's approach to optional-chained I/O.

conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. AddToShoppingListService.swift is a new file; no existing files were modified. Downstream UI integration beads (AddToShoppingListSheet, RecipeBottomBar) will need to import and call this service but do not touch the same file.

execution_history.summary: Created AddToShoppingListService.swift implementing the orchestration layer for appending recipe ingredients to shopping lists. The service provides two entry points: `append(recipe:scale:recipeName:to:aisleConfig:)` for existing lists and `create(recipe:scale:recipeName:named:in:aisleConfig:)` for new lists. Aisle mode detection via `isAisleBacked(_:)` inspects `##` sections for checklist-bearing content to distinguish aisle-structured lists from flat ones. Provenance bullet is written via `appendMealsBullet` before items in both flows. Build confirmed: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.
